source: LIVE GET https://algovault.com/api/performance-public (cache-busted). HTTP 200, 641693 B, application/json; charset=utf-8, NO cache-control header.
change_class: NO KEY CHANGE — the top-level key set is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 2026-07-15 snapshot allowed_keys (19). What this snapshot ADDS is a forbidden_values contract, the concept that snapshot lacked entirely.
change_note: This surface carries the estate performance data and was, until now, gated for VALUES by review alone. CLAUDE.md Data Integrity: outcome_return_pct / Phase E WR are INTERNAL ONLY and must never reach MCP/API/landing/README. That LAW was enforced on a DIFFERENT endpoint (/api/plans/public forbidden_keys) and by nobody here. It is now an executable assertion on the surface that actually carries performance data.
supersedes: audits/api-performance-public-shape-snapshot-2026-07-15.json — superseded, not edited away. That file is KEPT ON DISK and gains exactly TWO appended keys (superseded_by + superseded_reason) and nothing else; the per-file jq semantic-equality proof is in this wave CH3 gate. The append is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs projects EVERY audits/*-shape-snapshot-*.json into the PUBLIC knowledge bundle and src/lib/knowledge-index.ts keys each document response_shape:${endpoint}, so two LIVE files carrying /api/performance-public are a duplicate document id, which winkBM25S rejects outright: KnowledgeIndex.build() THROWS (Error: winkBM25S: Duplicate document encountered: response_shape:<endpoint>), tests/integration/knowledge-flow.test.ts fails, and at runtime the lazily-constructed index behind search_knowledge / chat_knowledge cannot be built. MEASURED CORRECTION, kept visible because the instrument matters: `npm run build:knowledge` TOLERATES the duplicate and exits 0 reporting response_shapes=39, so the builder succeeding is NOT evidence the bundle is usable — the rejection lives in the INDEX, not the build. A non-empty superseded_by is the ONLY thing that excludes a snapshot from that projection.

error_contract.description: Unchanged from 2026-07-15, restated as an OBJECT rather than a string. That is a FIX, not a reformat: scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs only projects error_contract when typeof === object, so the previous string was published into the public knowledge bundle as {} — a contract that said nothing.
error_contract.behaviour: Fail-open per-venue detector: byExchange degrades to empty, never 5xx. funding_venue_count is a compile-time constant (|FUNDING_VENUE_META|) and cannot fail at request time.

cache_contract.description: MEASURED 2026-09-10: NO cache-control header on this response (bucket-keyed rolling aggregate, in-process). The 2026-07-15 snapshot did not state the header either way.
cache_contract.staleness_signal: NONE. Do not key a freshness alarm on this body — CLAUDE.md: freshness alarms measure PRODUCERS, never rendered artifacts.

anchors_at_capture.note: Anchors, deliberately NOT a full captured_body — this response is 641693 B and embedding it would put a 640 KB duplicate of a live aggregate into the public knowledge bundle. The clean/violating PROOF PAIR below is the reviewable fixture; the REAL body is asserted by --live, which is the non-hermetic half.

forbidden_values._doc: Assertions are STRUCTURAL (path + predicate) or VALUE-REGEX over the stringified body, never a bare string ban. The absence rows use body_regex because this body nests 2134 distinct keys (byAsset alone contributes 2058 asset names), so a per-path enumeration would be unreviewable and would go stale the moment a venue is added. The positive rows use path + predicate, because THE OTHER DIRECTION is not optional: a contract that only forbids is satisfied by an endpoint that nulls every number.
forbidden_values.enforced_by: scripts/check-served-surface-values.mjs (SERVED_SURFACE_VALUES_VERDICT). live_only — reached by --live, scheduled as ops/cron/served-surface-values-canary.sh on signal-1. The clean/violating proof pair below runs OFFLINE in --self-test, which deploy.yml runs fail-closed.

assertions.reason: CLAUDE.md Data Integrity LAW: outcome WR is INTERNAL ONLY — outcome_return_pct / Phase E WR must NEVER be exposed via MCP/API/landing/README. Public is aggregated PFE WR only. This is that LAW as an executable assertion on the surface that actually carries performance data.

The 2026-07-15 forbidden_keys list, now enforced instead of documented. recentSignals is a teaser: id/coin/timeframe/tier/created_at/exchange. Publishing the verdict or its confidence here would give away the paid product, and signal_hash/merkle_root belong to the verify surface.
Per-signal excursion magnitudes are internal. The PUBLIC figure is the aggregated rate (overall.pfeWinRate), never the per-row return that produced it.
THE OTHER DIRECTION. Without it every absence row above is satisfied by an endpoint that returns {}. This is the headline the landing page and every data-tr-field consumer hydrate from.
The denominator behind the rate. A rate with no denominator is uncheckable, and the on-chain equality canary compares totalCalls against /api/merkle-batches total_signals.
Every one of these is a live data-tr-field target and a snapshot-landing-data.mjs injector source. Nulling one silently blanks a public number rather than failing loudly.
A published win rate with no methodology is a numerical-citation violation. The disclosure must travel with the number, on the same surface.

proof._doc:
R3.4 — a gate never observed catching the defect it was built for is not evidence. Both directions: the CLEAN body must produce ZERO violations, and the clean body with `mutations` APPLIED must be caught. Without the clean leg the proof is satisfied by a contract that fails on everything.
🛑 THE VIOLATING BODY IS DESCRIBED, NEVER STORED, AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE. Writing it out would put a literal `"outcome_return_pct": <number>` value binding into a tracked file in a PUBLIC repo — the exact shape the PII/secret-leak pre-push gate bans and the knowledge bundle's PII guard throws on. Measured: the first cut of this file was REFUSED by that gate, correctly. A mutation spec carries the key as a bare path element, so the banned shape is never written at all. --self-test applies these to a deep copy at runtime.

methodology.pfeWinRate: Peak Favorable Excursion win rate. Did price move in the signal direction at any point during the evaluation window?

mutations.why: the Data Integrity LAW: an internal realised return on a public surface
per-signal verdict leak — the paid product
THE OTHER DIRECTION: the surface nulls its own headline

drift_check._doc: NOT a drift_check_command shell string. That form was measured to have never run once — it was in no script, no workflow and no cron. This names an executable script and its verdict token.

modes.offline: NOT APPLICABLE to this surface. It is served from algovault.com and this repo exports no pure builder for it (measured: `export function build*Body` in src/ returns buildPublicPlansBody alone), so coverage is live_only. The clean/violating proof pair IS the offline leg.
modes.live: --live [baseUrl]. Fetches the deployed surface, cache-busted, and asserts these rules. SCHEDULED as ops/cron/served-surface-values-canary.sh, crontab 47 7 * * * on signal-1, alert SERVED_SURFACE_VALUE_DRIFT. A transport failure is INDETERMINATE, never FAIL.

proven_able_to_fail: The clean/violating pair above is executed by scripts/check-served-surface-values.mjs --self-test on every deploy. The mutations were observed producing violations before this file was committed; the clean body was observed producing none.
